tips.text: Legacy systems are just haunted houses with uptime requirements.
Tests are love letters to your future self.
Measure before you optimise — the ghost is usually in the query plan.
Boring code is good code.
Be kind to your code — it remembers everything.
Keep the receipts.
Hold the thread.
Exorcising legacy systems. Shipping code through the fog.
Migrations are rituals: rehearse them, then perform them once.
Ward your inputs — validate at the boundary, trust inside it.
You cannot banish a bug you have not named. Reproduce it first.
Small spells compose; giant incantations backfire.
A log line is a candle in the dark. Light the ones you will need at 3 a.m.
A runbook is a grimoire someone will read in a hurry. Write it plainly.
Never summon production without a circle drawn: backups, a plan, a way back.
A flaky test is a restless spirit. Find out what it is trying to tell you.
Before blaming the ORM, scry the EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
Global state is a curse that spreads to everything it touches.
Every deploy deserves a rollback charm.
Read the error message twice before casting anything new.
